sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Merchant Acquiring and Clearing Service Provider (PSP)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (modified Napoleonic Code with German doctrinal influence); unitary national system without sub-state corporate law distinction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: DTA Luxembourg–France (1958, as amended by the 2006 protocol)
DTA Luxembourg–United States (1996, as amended by the 2009 protocol)
DTA Luxembourg–United Kingdom (1968, as amended by the 2010 protocol)
TFEU/EU law framework: free movement of payment services under PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) and free movement of capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 13 January 2019 instituting the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and subsequent amendments; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML Law 2004); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT; Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended (PSD2 implementation); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010 on the AML Law 2004. Post-ECJ judgment of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20), the Luxembourg RBE is no longer fully public: competent authorities (CSSF, FIU, tax administration, bailiffs, notaries) and AML obliged entities conducting statutory customer due diligence retain access; the general public may obtain limited UBO data only upon demonstrated legitimate interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or extract from the foreign business/corporate register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961; Luxembourg acceded 1979); consular legalization required only if the origin state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration or foreign beneficial-ownership register excerpt evidencing the ultimate individuals behind each shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign UBO register or competent authority of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where a non-Apostille state is concerned; supplementary notarized certification before a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of constitutional documents (statuts/articles) and board/shareholder resolutions of the investing entities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (for the SARL deed) or foreign corporate register/notary (for shareholder resolutions)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign originals; Luxembourg notarial certification of copies for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of all UBOs, directors and managers (identity and residence evidence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing national authority of each individual; certification by a notary of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification plus Hague Apostille (where required by the receiving Luxembourg institution); consular legalization for non-Hague origin states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / police-clearance certificate (casier judiciaire) for proposed managers and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or police authority of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions; sworn translation into French, German, or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing source of funds for the initial share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signatory certification by the issuing bank; SWIFT/MT199 confirmation accepted in market practice; apostille only if expressly required by the receiving institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or notarially certified power of attorney granted to the Luxembourg incorporator/legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus Luxembourg sworn translation; consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and commercial counterparties against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Council Regulations (EU) No 765/2006 and 269/2014), (ii) UN Security Council consolidated list, (iii) US OFAC SDN list, and (iv) Luxembourg national asset-freezing measures published by the Ministry of Finance. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) determination per Article 1(19) of the AML Law 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, including family members and known close associates. Enhanced due diligence (source of wealth, source of funds, senior-management approval) is mandatory for any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction. Continuous transaction monitoring, risk-based periodic re-screening, and record retention of at least five years are required for a payment-service applicant.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (dénomination) must be expressed in Latin script, normally in French, German, or Luxembourgish; foreign-script names require Latin-alphabet transliteration. The name must be distinctive and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already registered in the RCS. A Société à Responsabilité Limitée must include the words 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the initials 'S.à r.l.' (or 'SARL') in the corporate name, and the RCS verifies legality, distinctiveness, and absence of prohibited tokens at filing. The notary performs an ex-ante availability search before deed execution.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Assurance / Réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization)
Payment Institution / Établissement de paiement / PSP (prior CSSF authorization under the Law of 10 November 2009)
Fonds / SICAV / SIF / FCP (CSSF collective-investment scheme authorization)
Réviseur d'entreprises (reserved for approved statutory auditors under the audit profession law)
Chambre de Commerce / Chambre des Métiers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a standalone public name-reservation register; the notary confirms availability ex ante, and the name is effectively secured by execution of the notarial deed, which must be filed with the RCS within one month (the 30-day window above). Upon a rejection (rejet) by the RCS registrar: (i) obtain the written grounds of refusal from the RCS; (ii) correct the name or the deed and re-present the dossier through the notary; (iii) if the registrar maintains the refusal, file an administrative appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within the statutory deadline, seeking an order to register; (iv) in the alternative, resubmit with a clearly distinguishable name avoiding the conflicting mark; service of the appeal on the RCS registrar and legal representation by a Luxembourg bar member are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Exceptional and substance-dependent: a pure virtual office is insufficient for a licensed payment institution, as the CSSF requires the head office (siège social et administration centrale) to be genuinely established in Luxembourg. A regulated domiciliation agent governed by the Law of 31 May 1999 may provide the registered address, but the PSP must maintain physical management premises, staff, IT infrastructure, and decision-making functions in Luxembourg. For a non-licensed passive holding SARL, commercial domiciliation is admissible, although tax-substance guidance recommends a real physical presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for the licensed PSP: estimated 65-75% probability of a planned or unannounced CSSF on-site inspection within 24 months of licence application or granting; AML/CFT thematic inspections by the CSSF are routine. For a passive holding SARL without a payment-services licence, the likelihood is materially lower, estimated at 10-20%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) including notarial identity and UBO verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif des notaires), scale-based; prevailing market range EUR 1,500-3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minimum share capital for SARL (EUR 12,000) blocked on notary client account pending RCS registration (not an expense; becomes company share capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (blocked capital account); released to the company upon RCS registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Article 710-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; statutory EUR 12,000 minimum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing fee and RESA publication (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory RCS tariff plus fixed RESA publication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copies of the notarial deed (copies exécutoires/certifiées) for foreign banks and regulators
Initial filing of the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) declaration with LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge; filed via notary or authorized intermediary

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg legal counsel: cross-border due diligence, UBO piercing analysis, drafting of articles, AML/CFT incorporation pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (member of the Luxembourg Bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 8,000-15,000 for Stage-1 incorporation and due-diligence package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CSSF pre-notification consultation (optional but recommended for the payment-institution licensing track under the Law of 10 November 2009)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) does not levy a pre-filing fee; amount covers counsel preparation and attendance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark hourly counsel fees for regulatory pre-application engagement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office and domiciliation agreement, first year (regulated domiciliation agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg domiciliation agent (regulated under Law of 31 May 1999)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff of EUR 100-150 per month depending on substance tier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign corporate, identity, and good-standing documents (bundle of 5-7 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authorities (Apostille per Hague Convention 1961); consular posts of non-Hague states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed international tariffs of USD 30-80 per document plus courier and handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of corporate and personal documents into French/German/English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff of EUR 15-35 per page depending on language pair and urgency

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC PEP and sanctions screening setup: database subscription activation and initial screening of UBOs, directors, and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial screening data provider / AML compliance consultancy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark covering initial PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Luxembourg consolidated-list sweeps plus onboarding configuration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 180-231 (SARL); Law of 19 August 2016 modernizing company law; Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services for licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating under the Ministry of Justice and managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of association (statuts constitutifs) together with the RCS incorporation form and required exhibits
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL statutory minimum capital is €12,000. Where the capital is exactly €12,000, it must be fully subscribed and fully paid up before registration; in all cases at least 25% of the nominal value of each share and the entire share premium must be paid. Paid-in funds must be deposited and blocked on an escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution until RCS registration and release order.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founder(s) having subscribed to the share capital, the payment gateway operating company shall be incorporated as a société à responsabilité limitée (SARL) under the Luxembourg Commercial Companies Law; that the draft articles of association be approved and executed; that the registered office be established at the address indicated in the articles; that the capital deposit escrow-bank release instruction be authorized upon RCS registration; that the persons named as managers (gérants) are appointed and dismissed powers confirmed; that banking mandates and cross-border payment gateway authorizations be opened; and that all filing formalities be completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) database / Ministry of Economy industry trade register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exhaustive search of the RCS and trademark records to confirm no conflicting corporate names. File a name reservation request with the RCS after notarized articles are signed; the notary automatically handles the reservation and registration. Adopt the legal entity identifier and verify acceptable corporate suffixes (SARL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is refused or conflicts, submit a newly selected name through the same notarial/RCS process; objection is cured by altering the style or adding a distinctive element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the full articles of association by the notary in accordance with the founders' instructions. The deed must identify all subscribers, corporate name, registered office, purpose, share capital, classes of shares, management structure, and the statutory audit details. Execute the deed before the notary; for SARL, if there are more than one founder, no deed by private signature is permitted; notarization is mandatory.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate confirming escrow deposit of share capital
Statement of no bankruptcy/criminal record for managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial queries must be resolved via supplementary declarations or corrected articles; the notary can file a new version within the same dossier without additional RCS fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the capital escrow account and depositing paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked reference account in the name of the 'société en formation' with a Luxembourg bank. Transfer the statutory minimum paid-up capital (€12,000 or more) by wire. Obtain a bank blocked-funds receipt to present to the notary. Upon RCS registration, the bank releases the funds to the company's current account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or refuses due diligence, accelerate by providing enhanced corporate records; use another Luxembourg credit institution and obtain an alternative blocked-funds certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and publication of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – RCS online portal / e-RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarized articles and exhibits with RCS on the e-RCS system. Pay the compulsory filing fee; RCS checks compliance, assigns an RCS number and numbers of the shares. After registration, the company acquires legal personality. The notary's filing publishes the incorporation in the official electronic compendium (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations – RESA) without delay.
required_dossiers: Declaration as to lawful activity (payment services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query or incomplete-file notice, the notary completes within 10 working days. Any misfiled registration can be rectified by filing a corrective annex to the articles or by RCS via court of commercial actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of managers, statutory declarations and opening the operational bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's shareholders in general meeting; Luxembourg Ministry of Economy (establishment permit); CSSF (payment institution license pre-application)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the first board resolution appointing gérants, whose mandate includes licensing applications. File confirmation declarations with the Trade and Companies Register for directors' identity. Submit business establishment permit application for payment services to the Ministry of Economy. Simultaneously file the payment institution license pre-application with CSSF.
required_dossiers: Identity and residence documents of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Management appointment defects are cured by a supplementary shareholders' resolution filed with RCS; CSSF deficiencies are addressed by submitting additional information within the legally prescribed investigation window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Division for Business Establishment (Direction générale de la légalisation) for the establishment permit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) and, separately, a payment institution (PI) authorisation licence issued by the CSSF

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity of online payment gateway services is not listed as a class 1 or 2 facility under the Grand-Ducal Regulations on environmental impact assessment; only a simplified administrative environmental registration is required if any on-premise activity is operated
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Given the non-industrial character, no wastewater/air emissions thresholds apply. For any server or office cooling equipment, compliance with Regulation (EU) 2024/573 on fluorinated greenhouse gases and with Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 July 2022 on energy performance of buildings. Waste handling must comply with the Luxembourg Waste Act of 21 March 2017, and producers must deliver electronics waste to approved recovery channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance must be obtained from the municipal authorities based on a report from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) verifying evacuation routes, extinguishers and alarm systems for the office/premises; structural load inspection is required only for buildings undergoing occupancy change; occupational clearance is issued by the Labour Inspectorate and Mines (Inspection du travail et des mines – ITM) confirming safe workstations, electrical installation compliance and emergency procedures prior to operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue – Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; VAT and registration taxes – Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Customs – Administration des douanes et accises. Electronic access: MyGuichet.lu single e-government portal and eCDF electronic VAT filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity: (1) register the legal entity with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) or register a Luxembourg branch; (2) RCS filing automatically creates a national business identification number (NRC) used as the tax file number with the ACD; (3) apply to AED for a VAT number using Form 1600, attaching articles of association, RCS extract, and proof of foreign tax residency; a tax representative may be required for non-established providers; (4) complete social security registration with the Common Centre of Social Security (CCSS) if carrying on Luxembourg activity. Foreign entities with no Luxembourg establishment supplying B2B services from abroad generally do not need Luxembourg VAT registration for input VAT recovery unless Luxembourg is the place of supply under the reverse-charge mechanism.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law does not offer a check-the-box or partnership-style transparency election for a SARL. A SARL is a capital company taxable at entity level. Available elective mechanisms include: (i) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) pursuant to Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for related established taxable persons; (ii) corporate income tax fiscal unity for 95%-owned Luxembourg tax-resident subsidiaries under Section 164bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law; (iii) application for an advance tax ruling from the Luxembourg Tax Authorities to confirm financing structures, hybrid characterization, or participation exemption treatment; (iv) ATAD hybrid-mismatch neutralisation rules may be triggered by elective transparent/investment entity classifications recognised by another Member State, but Luxembourg itself does not provide a unilateral check-the-box election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for supplies of goods and services in Luxembourg; the threshold does not apply to non-established taxable persons when the place of supply is Luxembourg or when the reverse-charge mechanism applies; intra-Community acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000 and distance sales or electronically supplied services under EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) regimes may trigger registration obligations outside Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time VAT clearance, fiscal stamping, or continuous transaction control regime is currently in force in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is mandatory exclusively for B2G transactions and must use the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 interoperable format through the Luxembourg e-Submission platform. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary. VAT returns and EC Sales Lists are submitted electronically through eCDF (Electronic Cash Desk and Filing) on MyGuichet.lu; there is no public mandatory API clearance mandate beyond authenticated XML/e-Submission for government contracts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: export of goods to a non-EU state qualifies for 0% VAT if the goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU and the supplier or its agent retains authoritative proof of export; intra-Community supplies to a taxable person in another EU Member State are zero-rated subject to the customer's valid VAT ID, EC Sales List, and transport evidence. Services: B2B payment gateway, merchant acquiring, and digital intermediary services supplied to a customer in another jurisdiction generally fall outside Luxembourg VAT through the reverse-charge mechanism in the customer's jurisdiction; financial services, including payment intermediation and clearing by an authorised PSP, are VAT-exempt under Article 43 of the Luxembourg VAT Law implementing Article 135(1)(d) of the EU VAT Directive. Services physically rendered to non-EU recipients and directly connected with exported goods may also be zero-rated. No PSP service is automatically zero-rated unless the specific supply falls within an expressly exempt or outside-scope rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Accompanying Document / MRN confirmation)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR transport document with proof of physical departure from the EU
Commercial Invoice issued by the Luxembourg exporter
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT proof of foreign exchange receipt
Signed contract evidencing risk, ownership, and control of the export transaction
Customer identity and economic-residence evidence for B2B services, including reverse-charge validation records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may withdraw zero-rating or the applicable exemption where transport or customs documentation is missing or inconsistent, issuing assessments for unpaid VAT plus default interest. Administrative fines for documentary non-compliance can reach EUR 4,000; in cases of deliberate fraud, tax evasion, or use of false export declarations, criminal penalties include imprisonment up to five years and fines proportional to the evaded tax, with retrospective reassessment under the anti-abuse doctrine and the standard ten-year statute of limitations for indirect tax offences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign-exchange policy and monetary sovereignty are exercised through the ECB for euro-area matters and the BCL for national statistical, supervisory, and account-holding functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg provides full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63 and 64 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No exchange licence, approval mechanism, or discriminatory currency rationing exists for payment services, direct investment, or profit remittances. Cross-border transfers in EUR or any other currency are unrestricted except where applicable EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering (AML/CFT) controls, or customs/counter-terrorist financing rules impose screening obligations. Dividend remittances from a Luxembourg SARL are subject to the 15% domestic withholding tax on distributions, but the rate can be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or to treaty rates under most Luxembourg double tax treaties where beneficiary conditions are satisfied. Capital repatriation on liquidation is generally not subject to withholding tax beyond the taxation of accumulated profits. The practical hurdles are statistical rather than regulatory: resident companies must report cross-border payments and external financial assets/liabilities to BCL for the compilation of the Luxembourg balance of payments, typically through the current account, financial account, and direct investment reporting forms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion obligations on export proceeds in Luxembourg. Resident companies may retain, borrow against, transfer, or freely convert any foreign currency earnings into EUR or other currencies without a timeline or a conversion ratio. For balance-of-payments statistical completeness, BCL requires that enterprises directly report each cross-border transaction above the prevailing reporting threshold (individually or annually, depending on the nature and counterparty country) and that foreign receivables and payables outstanding be reported through BCL's external asset/liability survey schemas. Failure to file accurate BCL returns may expose the company to administrative fines, but this is a reporting duty, not an exchange control limit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for EU-authorized electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions (PIs) that passport into Luxembourg under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2/EU 2015/2366). Such entities may hold a Luxembourg license from the CSSF or a comparable license in another EU/EEA state and may open settlement accounts with local banks and directly access SEPA, SWIFT, and card clearing systems. Feasibility rating: Low for offshore digital EMIs headquartered outside the European Economic Area; they cannot passport under PSD2 and would require either a Luxembourg-authorised subsidiary, a branch licence, or a partnership with a licensed EU PI/EMI. The legal constraints include the prohibition on deposit-taking, the requirement to safeguard client funds through segregated accounts, the mandatory capital and own-funds requirements (initial capital of EUR 350,000 for an EMI, EUR 125,000 for a PI), and CSSF regulatory notification before using agents or outsourcing critical operational functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Luxembourg AML legislation (Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended) and CSSF Circular 12/552, customer due diligence must be performed with reliable, independent-source documentary evidence. Physical presence is not an absolute statutory requirement for opening a corporate account if a qualified electronic identification signature (eIDAS) and an in-person-verified video conference are used. However, for a high-risk commercial model such as a cross-border payment service provider, virtually all tier-1 Luxembourg banks require one or more natural persons — typically the CEO, a director, and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) — to attend a physical interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises or at the Luxembourg notary's office. A remote opening alternative may be accepted in narrow cases involving a pre-existing long-term credit relationship, but for fresh SARL incorporations, physical attendance is the de facto mandate. The interview may be conducted via a live video link only after a local counsel or a bank representative has performed a face-to-face verification; in practice, this is rarely granted for overseas UBOs on day one.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The corporate purpose is an online merchant acquiring and clearing service provider, carrying an inherent high-risk payment-intermediary profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF payment-institution or e-money-institution licence or a formal application in advanced stage; a complete AML/CFT compliance manual; a documented transaction-monitoring system with case-management workflow; a safeguards policy for merchant funds; a sanctions and PEP screening procedure; audited financial projections evidencing transaction volumes and expected monthly wire flows; appointment of an AML compliance officer with demonstrated professional competence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows to and from merchants in multiple non-EU jurisdictions, raising correspondent-bank de-risking and jurisdictional risk flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A merchant due-diligence playbook with risk-scoring matrices; country-by-country exposure limits; evidence of registration with Luxembourg’s Trade and Companies Register (RCS); a description of underlying commercial contracts; a map of correspondent banking chains, including the name of each intermediary IBAN/SWIFT routing; a clear rationale for each non-EU market, plus the licences held in each destination or statements that no regulated activity is performed there.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO structure involves multi-jurisdictional holding entities, potential nominee shareholders, or non-transparent trusts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A core 100% UBO chain tracing each entity to natural persons; authenticated copies of incorporation documents and shareholder registers from the entire corporate chain; a Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract within 10 business days of data submission; declarations from directors and shareholders confirming industrial property; passports and utility bills for all natural-person UBOs; a signed power-of-attorney register and a negative-declaration form if no UBO exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds details for the statutory minimum capital and subsequent operating liquidity are considered opaque, particularly where funds originate from a foreign parent group.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised deed certifying the subscription and payment of share capital; the bank’s blocked-account attestation; a shareholder resolution approving the capital increase; the original wire or SWIFT MT103 confirming the movement of funds; for parent-group injections, a board resolution, an equity contribution agreement, a short-term intercompany loan agreement, and consolidated financial statements evidencing the legitimate economic substance of the funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from non-resident shareholders must be executed through SWIFT wire transfers (MT103) to the SARL's Luxembourg capital-escrow or operational account. The sender must use the company’s exact FX-efficient EUR IBAN with no intermediate account and provide an explicit wire reference in field 70 such as 'Share Capital Contribution under Resolution dated [date]' or 'Capital increase SARL [name]'. The receiving bank will require a copy of the notarised board/shareholder resolution and an updated RCS extract after registration. Where the shareholder is a holding company in a tax treaty jurisdiction, the bank also requests the corporate tax registration and proof of real economic activity to validate treaty-based withholding rules. The BCL balance-of-payments report must classify the incoming amount under direct investment equity capital, with counterparty country and BIC/IBAN details, by the 10th business day after the month of receipt at the corporate's reporting portal.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The SARL uses multi-rail clearing for trade and merchant settlements: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated EEA transactions, using the debtor’s and creditor’s IBAN with standard SEPA purpose codes; (2) SWIFT MT103/M202 for payments outside the EEA or non-EUR currency, routed via a Luxembourg bank or its correspondents; (3) commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) opened by the Luxembourg bank in favour of overseas sellers, especially for high-value or documentary trade flows; (4) payment card clearing through Visa/Mastercard settlement reports, with funding to acquiring banks, generally via SWIFT MT202 COV or the Fedwire system for USD balances; and (5) local instant clearing (LuxSEA) where high daily frequency requires batch settlement. For treasury control, outbound disbursements must be pre-authorised under a four-eyes principle, matched against the procurement or merchant agreement, and reported to BCL under the monthly balance-of-payments survey with the corresponding counterparty sector and country.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) executed with a Luxembourg bank or EU-authorised broker, provided the notional does not exceed the SARL’s measured currency exposure and the instrument is booked for cash-flow hedging.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to convertibility restrictions or price controls, settling in EUR on a spot reference date, and permissible under Luxembourg law when the counterparty is licensed under EU MiFID II/CASS custody rules.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) matching the tenor and coupon of underlying trade finance or capital structure, fully hedged on a natural cash-flow basis.
FX swaps (swap transactions involving simultaneous spot sale/purchase and forward re-purchase) for intraday or 48-hour funding relief, with the economic substance being purely liquidity management.

European-style FX options purchased or sold in tandem with an independent risk committee mandate, strictly hedge-only, and prohibited for speculative trading unless separately authorised by a future CSSF licence for portfolio management.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS confirmation statement (déclaration annuelle) confirming company particulars and UBO details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary of the RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of approximately EUR 125 per occurrence; repeated non-compliance triggers administrative strike-off from the RCS and may result in judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss, notes and management report) filed and published
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year end (e.g., by 31 July for a calendar-year SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors subject to criminal fines of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000; failure to file for three consecutive years triggers compulsory dissolution or strike-off after formal warning.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual tax return for corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (ICC), and net wealth tax (IFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December of the year following the tax year (for calendar-year accounts); e-filing extensions may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month, late-submission penalties of up to EUR 1,000, and administrative tax assessment based on estimated income where no return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation and beneficial ownership declaration update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the annual RCS confirmation statement, no later than one month after the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment for directors; restrictions on corporate acts and distribution of dividends.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual compliance and financial report to the financial sector supervisory authority (payment institution reporting)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after financial year end (31 March for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CSSF enforcement actions including licence suspension or revocation, administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover, and prohibition on providing payment services.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds any two of the following thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average number of employees 50; however, a licensed payment institution is subject to mandatory audit irrespective of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and annual accounts, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts; additional CSSF reporting formats apply for payment institutions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the SARL must confirm through the LBR annual declaration the identity of its ultimate beneficial owners and any changes; any transfer resulting in a 25% or greater shareholding or voting right must be reported to the RBE within 30 days; the share transfer register is updated contemporaneously.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined effective headline rate for Luxembourg City, FY2024: 17% corporate income tax (IRC) + 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC + 6.75% municipal business tax (TASOC); FY2025 combined rate reduced to 23.94% following IRC decrease to 16%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% exemption on qualifying IP income, including copyrighted payment-software, producing an effective combined IP rate of approx. 4.99% FY2024 and 4.79% FY2025; 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% shareholding and 12-month holding period, or EUR 1.2 million acquisition price); no general tax holiday for payment institutions, but R&D tax credit is available for qualifying fintech software development.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 500 (corporate income tax and net wealth tax declaration) and Formulaire 5 (municipal business tax declaration) filed electronically via the Luxembourg Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) e-filing portal accessible through MyGuichet.lu / e-CDF.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory filing deadline is 30 April of the calendar year following the tax year-end; a six-month extension is available upon written request to the ACD; for electronically filed corporate returns, administrative practice generally permits a deferred due date of 31 December of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, RCS number, LEI, registered office, tax ID, business activity (ISIC 6619 / Payment Service Provider), and CSSF licence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must identify the PE address, local tax representative, and certify that Luxembourg-source acquiring and gateway fees are attributed to the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 2 - Fiscal Year and Accounting Basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the tax year, applicable GAAP, currency conversion if accounts are kept in a foreign currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must present Luxembourg PE profit prepared under LUX GAAP, with clear mapping from foreign GAAP and EUR conversion notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial profit before statutory tax adjustments, computed after depreciation, provisions, and ordinary operating expenses of the PSP gateway business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically connected to the Luxembourg PE are deductible; head-office cost allocations must be documented under transfer pricing standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption deductions, IP box deduction (80% of qualifying IP income), tax-exempt transactional income, and applicable loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders utilising Luxembourg participation exemption must attach evidence of shareholding percentage, holding period, and beneficial ownership; IP box claims require DEMPE documentation in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income subject to IRC, solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax; declaration of any payments subject to withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must declare any Luxembourg-source dividend, interest, or royalty flows and certify whether domestic exemption or DTA relief was applied at source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a formal reminder, followed by an estimated administrative assessment; a late-filing/late-payment surcharge of 10% on the assessed tax is applied, together with default interest of 0.6% per commenced month; incomplete or missing TP documentation attracts administrative fines of EUR 250 to EUR 4,000; intentional non-filing or false declarations constitute tax fraud punishable by a fine of up to five times the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (WHT) on distributions by a SARL; reduced to 0% where the parent qualifies under the Luxembourg participation exemption or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (minimum 10% capital, 12-month holding period); treaty rates for non-resident corporate shareholders generally 0% or 5%, portfolio shareholders 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1. Non-resident beneficial owner obtains an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC / certificat de résidence fiscale) from the home tax administration. 2. The TRC, accompanied by a beneficial-ownership statement and shareholding history, is submitted to the Luxembourg distributing SARL before the dividend payment date using the ACD exoneration form. 3. The Luxembourg paying entity withholds at the treaty-reduced rate (0% or 5%) or at zero under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the conditions are satisfied. 4. If excess WHT is withheld, a refund claim must be filed with the ACD within three years of 31 December of the distribution year, supported by certified TRC evidence. 5. For third-country treaty applications, additional legalisation or apostille may be required depending on the bilateral convention.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose domestic withholding tax on outbound royalty payments, including software, IP licence fees, or on outbound interest payments on loans, bonds, or bank deposits; therefore no source-state DTA relief protocol is required for such streams; however, remuneration re-characterised as a constructive dividend remains subject to the 15% domestic dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the Luxembourg SARL's annual gross consideration for related-party transactions equals or exceeds EUR 1,000,000; Master File is mandatory where the worldwide consolidated group net turnover reaches EUR 750,000,000; below these thresholds the OECD contemporaneous documentation standard still applies on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but economic substance is enforced through the ATAD Article 6 General Anti-Abuse Rule, the administrative substance doctrine applied by the Luxembourg Ruling Committee, the requirement to satisfy treaty-beneficial-ownership tests, and the CSSF prudential licensing regime for payment institutions under PSD2; a SARL that is a letter-box PSP with no local decision-making, risk management, full-time staff, or office infrastructure will be disregarded and profits reattributed to the foreign principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to declare cross-border merchant acquiring and settlement fees; diverting interchange income to offshore shell accounts; issuing false B2B invoices; maintaining no genuine Luxembourg management or operational substance to disguise the real source of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment of undeclared IRC, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; 10% late-filing surcharge; default interest at 0.6% per commenced month; criminal fine of up to five times the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years before the Tribunal d'arrondissement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Gérants and directors face personal criminal liability for tax fraud, civil restitution of evaded tax, joint and several liability for corporate tax debts where the veil is pierced, asset seizures, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a mere booking plant with no resident directors, no operational offices, no locally controlled payment functions, and funneling all profits to a non-resident affiliate while invoking treaty benefits or the participation exemption without genuine beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment with denial of the participation exemption and treaty benefits; reclassification of profit repatriation as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT; 10% penalty surcharge; fines for prohibited shell arrangements under Luxembourg and EU anti-avoidance frameworks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Luxembourg courts will pierce the corporate veil where separate legal personality is a pure façade; directors and shadow directors are civilly liable for the shortfall, may be subject to travel bans, freezing orders, and up to five years imprisonment for abusive fraud or false attestation.
